title: Rigveda 9.47: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.47: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.47 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 685v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.47.1-5 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 4); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 685v
translation.original_text:
1a̱yā soma̍ḥ sukṛ̱tyayā̍ ma̱haś ci̍d a̱bhy a̍vardhata | ma̱ndā̱na ud vṛ̍ṣāyate ||
2kṛ̱tānīd a̍sya̱ kartvā̱ ceta̍nte dasyu̱tarha̍ṇā | ṛ̱ṇā ca̍ dhṛ̱ṣṇuś ca̍yate ||
3āt soma̍ indri̱yo raso̱ vajra̍ḥ sahasra̱sā bhu̍vat | u̱kthaṁ yad a̍sya̱ jāya̍te ||
4sva̱yaṁ ka̱vir vi̍dha̱rtari̱ viprā̍ya̱ ratna̍m icchati | yadī̍ marmṛ̱jyate̱ dhiya̍ḥ ||
5si̱ṣā̱satū̍ rayī̱ṇāṁ vāje̱ṣv arva̍tām iva | bhare̍ṣu ji̱gyuṣā̍m asi ||
translation.text:
1GREAT as he was, Soma hath gained strength by this high solemnity: joyous he riseth like a bull.
2His task is done: his crushings of the Dasyus are made manifest: He sternly reckoneth their debts.
3Soon as his song of praise is born, the Soma, Indra's juice, becomes A thousand-winning thunderbolt.
4Seer and Sustainer, he himself desireth riches for the sage When he embellisheth his songs.
5Fain would they both win riches as in races of the steeds. In war Thou art upon the conquerors' side.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 685v (numbered 2v by the scribe) (OPenn image 686, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.46.3 ‹karma-bhiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 686r (numbered 3r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.48.3 ‹rayim abhi rājānam sukrato›. Verses 9.47.1-5 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1ayā | somaḥ | su-kṛtyayā | mahaḥ | cit | abhi | avardhata | mandānaḥ | ut | vṛṣa-yate
2kṛtāni | it | asya | kartvā | cetante | dasyu-tarhaṇā | ṛṇā | ca | dhṛṣṇuḥ | cayate
3āt | somaḥ | indriyaḥ | rasaḥ | vajraḥ | sahasra-sāḥ | bhuvat | uktham | yat | asya | jāyate
4svayam | kaviḥ | vi-dhartari | viprāya | ratnam | icchati | yadi | marmṛjyate | dhiyaḥ
5sisāsatuḥ | rayīṇām | vājeṣu | arvatām-iva | bhareṣu | jigyuṣām | asi
